title: introduce-chain-aware-span-grouper-and-stream-cost-adapter
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add chain-aware span grouping for streamed responses and a lightweight stream-cost adapter to approximate per-token cost on partial/chunked responses. Improves trace readability and enables token-cost breakdowns for long streaming sessions.
description: Motivation: Streaming responses and multi-turn chains produce lots of small spans and partial tokens, which makes trace graphs noisy and costs hard to attribute. Customers running chat-heavy workloads asked for clearer trace grouping and approximate per-token costing for streamed chunks so ops can debug and attribute spend without having to rehydrate full sessions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a chain-aware span grouper in the tracing pipeline that coalesces consecutive spans belonging to the same logical chain/session into a single rollup span with aggregated metrics and deterministic keys; and 2) a Stream Cost Adapter that consumes chunked/partial token events and emits ephemeral cost-attribution metrics with conservative heuristics (prefix-fractioning + model-profile weights) so dashboards can show near-real-time token-costs for streaming responses. Checklist: - [x] Implement span grouper and config flags - [x] Add stream-cost adapter with pluggable model weight table - [x] Expose metrics: stream_tokens_total, stream_token_cost_estimate, chain_span_length, chain_span_error_rate - [x] Wire OTEL span attributes for chain_id, chain_role, chunk_index - [x] Add unit and integration tests for grouping heuristics - [x] Console dashboard: chain stream-cost view + example alert rules - [x] Backfill migration script: noop safe default - [x] Docs: observability streaming guide Summary of changes: Commits: - a9f3b9c: initial implementation of chain-aware span grouper (core logic + unit tests) - b4d1e2f: add stream cost adapter, model weight table, and conservative heuristics - c2d4a88: metrics export hooks and Prometheus labels for chain_id/model - d9f7b1a: add console dashboard JSON and alert example - e1b7f04: tests and CI fixes + docs updates Files changed (high level): - tracing/span_grouper.py: core grouping algorithm and deterministic key derivation - tracing/tests/test_span_grouper.py: unit tests that exercise boundary conditions - observability/stream_cost_adapter.py: adapter that converts partial chunk events into token-cost estimates - metrics/exporters/prometheus_chain_exporter.py: export hooks with chain labels - console/dashboards/chain_stream_cost.json: dashboard definition + example widgets - docs/observability/streaming-traces.md: how it works, tuning knobs, and migration notes - infra/ci/test_observability.sh: new test harness for integration run - examples/streaming/README.md: quickstart and expected traces Review/Conversation: - Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two requests: (1) make the group key stable across retries so we can join traces in storage, (2) add a note about accuracy bounds for the stream cost heuristic." - Author (Maya): "Added deterministic nonce derivation so group keys are stable when upstream request_id is present; otherwise we derive from session fingerprint. Also added a short accuracy section to docs listing our conservative +/-10–25% bound depending on model/quantization." - Priya Nandakumar (reviewer): "CI caught a flaky integration test on bursty streams — tracing pipeline was dropping some chunks under high concurrency." - Author (Maya): "Fixed: increased internal buffer window and added backpressure metrics. Re-ran integration; green locally." - Samir Patel (final approver): "Approach looks sound; leaving a couple of nit comments on logging verbosity." CI Summary: - unit tests: pass - lint: pass - integration (observability suite): initial run failed (trace_buffer_overflow flaky) -> buffer window increased and test retried -> pass - e2e smoke: pass Note on accuracy and safety: The Stream Cost Adapter is intentionally conservative: it attributes fractional token counts for partial chunks and multiplies by model-weight factors from the model profile table. We label these metrics with attribute cost_estimate=approximate and provide a confidence tag (high/medium/low) so alerting can ignore low-confidence metrics. Default behavior is opt-in via observability.enable_stream_cost_adapter=false to avoid surprising billing spikes for customers who rely on exact billing. Configuration and tuning: - observability.span_grouper.enabled (bool, default true) - observability.span_grouper.max_merge_window_ms (int, default 300) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.enabled (bool, default false) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.model_weight_table (config map) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.confidence_threshold (float, default 0.6) Backwards compatibility and migration: - Grouping is additive at the tracing ingest layer; original fine-grained spans are still stored for 7 days controlled by observability.span_grouper.keep_fine_spans_days (default 7) so users can revert. - Stream cost adapter metrics are namespaced with stream_ prefix and do not feed billing pipelines unless an explicit opt-in flag is set. Rollout plan: - Canary on a small subset of hosted region (10% of streaming traffic) for 48 hours - Monitor chain_span_length, stream_token_cost_estimate, trace_error_rate - If no regressions (latency or spike in metric cardinality) after 48h, increase to 50% and run full canary window - GA after two successful canaries and customer docs updated Observability dashboards and alerts added: - New dashboard: "Chain Stream Cost (Canary)" with per-model cost estimates and chain latency histograms - New alert: "StreamCost: high-unattributed-variance" (fires when estimate variance > 40% for 10m) - New alert: "TraceGrouping: buffer-saturation" (fires on buffer occupancy > 85%) Known limitations and follow-ups: - Edge cases where upstream partial retransmits can double-count chunks; follow-up ticket ENG-3310 to add idempotency tags - Model-profile table is conservative and needs periodic calibration; follow-up ENG-3312 to add automated calibration job - Large cardinality risk: chain_id labels increase high-cardinality metrics; we implemented a capped cardinality rollup and will monitor; follow-up ENG-3313 to add reservoir sampling for low-traffic chains Merge: Squash-merged to main after reviewers approved and CI green. Notes: small telemetry spike observed during canary but within expectations. Docs, tests and dashboard JSONs included so console team can iterate.
